text.p: The remains of Tropical Cyclone 06B continue to cause locally heavy showers in Bangladesh, where flooding has occurred. Conditions should improve as showers end this period.

Tropical Depression 34W is moving northwestward in the Gulf of Thailand, and though weak, should produce heavy showers and local flash flooding over the Malay Peninsula this period. It will then move into the Andaman Sea of the Bay of Bengal and may intensify into an important tropical cyclone.
Tropical Cyclone 05A is moving westward in the Arabian Sea. It should dissipate east of northern Somalia in 36-48 hours, threatening only shipping.

Tropical Cyclone 05S will become an increasing threat to shipping in the Indian Ocean. The storm is centered near 10.6s/96.7e, moving south at 6 mph, and is expected to turn to the west this period. Top winds are 40 mph but are expected to increase to 60 mph during the next 48 hours.

A strong storm system over the north central USA is causing strong winds. On the western and northern side of this storm, cold air and snow is occurring. Very cold air in the upper Plains of the USA may lead to early-season cold-related problems through Thursday. The cold air will then move into the Midwest and will cause some problems.
